# Spells #533 fixtures

Exactly the 100 ordered root Spell records from #533, plus complete pinned Spell reference bodies, class records used for class-tag lookup, seven owned class features and one Technology Journal used solely for evidence. Source manifests retain empty pack directories. These fixtures are isolated import and saved-sheet specimens; none confers catalog admission.

`provenance.json` commits original file bytes, ordered keys, manifests, class context and the independently fetched PCGen files. `preview.json` contains the exact selected scope. `binding-preview.json` contains the complete reference context used to bind all root assessments. `bibliography-source.txt` is source-identity evidence only and never imported as runtime code. Bibliography quotes identify publications; they do not prove rules or complete notice chains.

The owning review is `scripts/catalog/legal/spells-533.json`. Every whole-content and record-level3.5 hold remains unresolved. Unexpanded governing bodies, partial PCGen creature rows, missing complete bodies and manual mechanics are identified separately; none is called a complete composed or executed effect.

`preserved.json` freezes every previous raw/runtime shared row and all8,314 fixture blobs. `protected-context.json` freezes the historical complete-definition union before optional outputs are added. `verification.json`, `local-binding-proof.json` and `historical-binding-proof.json` record fresh source, separate local and combined complete proof scopes, covering all4,031 historical bindings. Full CLI artifacts and complete input/output ledgers are archived by the orchestration lane; they are not committed wholesale here.

`sheet.ts` builds recorded-Spell specimens through the public resolver. The batch integration tests install only into an isolated convex-test Character catalog, exercise authorized/public writes and reads and legal release transport, and prove no passive bonuses, running Spell Effects or held shipping definitions are created. No production or remote deployment is involved.
